mari: Thinking about the RFC follow-up — can we safely multiplex connections between the front proxy and adapters so we don't consume one socket per tenant?
aj: short answer: yes, but there are tradeoffs. multiplexing reduces socket pressure but complicates auth/kv cache semantics.
jamie: agree. main concerns: (1) how do we keep per-tenant KV cache correctness, (2) how to propagate tenant identity for auditing, (3) head-of-line blocking.
toby: HTTP/2 or gRPC streams give multiplexing and per-stream metadata (headers) which helps identity propagation. but some private deployments (air-gapped sidecars) don't want/have gRPC support.
mari: for Private we can't change the customer's sidecar easily. We need a design that works for hosted + dedicated + private with minimal behavior deltas.
aj: proposal: do multiplexing at the front-proxy <-> adapter boundary when adapter declares capability "stream-multiplex: true". If not declared, fall back to 1:1 sockets.
jamie: yeah capability negotiation feels right. Also need a clear contract for cache invalidation: if two tenants share the same TCP connection in a multiplexing flow, their KV cache keys must be namespaced and eviction must include tenant context.
sera: security/PII note: TLS termination point matters. If we terminate TLS at front-proxy and then multiplex to adapters over an internal channel, audit events must include original TLS client cert/thumbprint or forwarded token. We need to avoid relying on opaque internal headers for auth decisions.
aj: agreed — we should propagate signed token proof (short-lived) per stream. something like: x-tenant-auth: bearer <short_jwt> with a signature that adapters can validate against control-plane pubkey.
toby: that works for hosted/dedicated. For Private where control plane is customer-managed, we need a pluggable verification endpoint or local CA bundle. add capability "auth-verify-mode: local|remote" to manifest.
mari: performance: multiplexing reduces syscalls and memory for sockets, but increases per-stream scheduling overhead. any numbers?
jamie: quick microbench: gRPC multiplexing on our infra reduced peak FDs by ~7x and improved p95 latency for small requests by ~10%, but increased 99.9th by ~5% due to cross-tenant queues. Head-of-line can be mitigated with per-tenant priority queues and strict per-tenant concurrency limits.
aj: operational model: when multiplexed, we need to expose per-stream telemetry (tokens/latency/cost) to Console. That requires the proxy to attach stream metadata to traces. We already have tracing hooks, but need a consistent stream id -> tenant mapping.
jamie: also need meaningful fallbacks: if an adapter misbehaves under multiplex, we should be able to quiesce only affected streams, not kill the whole connection. That implies the runtime must support per-stream health and circuit breakers.
ops-bot: deploy pipeline: canary rollout of multiplexing-capable front-proxy to staging at 2026-03-20T12:00Z :rocket:
mari: config example idea:

```yaml
adapter_capabilities:
  - name: streaming
    stream_multiplex: true
    auth_verify_mode: remote
    max_streams_per_connection: 512
    per_tenant_concurrency: 8

```

aj: that config covers a lot. we should add `kv_namespace_mode: namespaced|shared` with default `namespaced` to force tenant key isolation in shared connections.
sera: add `audit_binding: include_client_cert|include_token` so auditors can assert where the principal came from.
toby: corner case: long-running generation streams where KV cache (KV = prefetched prefixes) is large — multiplexing can cause memory bloat if caches are kept warm per-stream. suggestion: keep a lightweight per-tenant descriptor in the proxy and only materialize large KV caches in adapters on demand.
jamie: yup — lazy materialization. and an eviction policy keyed by last-accessed stream to avoid OOM.
mari: what about sticky routing for latency-sensitive tenants (dedicated customers)? multiplexing may introduce jitter from shared scheduling.
aj: add `routing_policy: sticky|balanced`. default balanced for cost-efficiency. customers with SLA can request sticky sessions (1:1) or reserved streams.
sera: audit/security: make sure capability negotiation and metadata headers are mutually authenticated. don't accept `stream-multiplex: true` from an adapter unless its identity is verified via mTLS or signed capability manifest.
ops-bot: canary logs show no auth regression on staging. token propagation via x-tenant-auth validated by adapters (staging) at 1763570300.
toby: implementation note: use a short-lived stream token with a nonce bound to the control-plane-issued session. That avoids replay.
mari: open questions we should capture for RFC appendix: 1) default per-tenant concurrency; 2) eviction thresholds for lazy KV; 3) what metrics we surface to Console for multiplexed streams; 4) Private deployment verification flow (local vs remote).
aj: I'll draft a short follow-up RFC section with config knobs and a migration plan: two-week canary -> opt-in for Dedicated -> opt-in for Private customers after testing.
jamie: +1. Also include a small compatibility shim: `proxy_mode: multiplex|legacy` that operator can flip per-proxy.
mari: ok. next action items: aj to draft RFC patch, jamie to add perf microbench with per-tenant priority queues, sera to write security checklist for signed stream tokens. target review EOD Friday. :calendar: :white_check_mark:
aj: I'll have the patch by Thursday noon.
